attribution.title: Merseyside Maritime Museum, Albert Dock, Liverpool - geograph.org.uk - 633029
attribution.author: Stephen Guy
attribution.description: Merseyside Maritime Museum, Albert Dock, Liverpool One of Europe's largest maritime museums housed in a Grade I-listed former warehouse designed and built by Jesse Hartley in 1846. Includes historic vessels and two historic quaysides. The displays reflect the history of the merchant navy, shipping from the 13th century and the development of the Port of Liverpool and its international links. The International Slavery Museum, opened in August 2007 on the third floor, tells the story of the transatlantic slave trade up to its abolition in 1807.

attribution.title: Williamson Tunnels - The Banqueting Hall
attribution.author: Kyle J May
attribution.description:
Apr 2019. The 'Banqueting Hall' beneath the site of Joseph Williamson's house, Mason Street, Liverpool. This was likely built as a sandstone quarry and vaulted over in the early 19th century by Williamson. There are work lights, cones and a distant scaffold platform visible as this is still an active dig site, with excavations continuing in a chamber off the right hand wall (behind and below the red barrier). 
Photo by Kyle May, Friends Of Williamson's Tunnels.
